mainTopic: A woman redeeming מעשר שני (holy vs. ordinary property), and freeing an עבד כנעני through tooth, eye and limb-tips
overview: The amud opens with a ברייתא about a woman redeeming מעשר שני. The תנא קמא says she must add a fifth (חומש), while רבי שמעון בן אלעזר in the name of רבי מאיר says she does not. The גמרא rejects two possible cases and settles on one where someone gave her money on condition that she redeem the מעשר with it. In that case the opinions seem to be the reverse of what רבי מאיר and the חכמים said in the earlier slave case. אביי answers that we should swap the opinions. רבא keeps them as they are: the מעשר came from her father's house, and the two sides argue whether מעשר is sacred property, which the husband never acquires, or ordinary property, which he does. The גמרא then turns to a new ברייתא: an עבד כנעני goes free if his master destroys his tooth, his eye, or the tips of limbs that do not grow back. The limb-tips are learned from tooth and eye, which are visible, permanent blemishes. The גמרא challenges this with the rule of 'two verses that come as one' and begins to show that both were needed, an answer that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A ברייתא on a woman redeeming second tithe
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא says a woman redeems מעשר שני only with a חומש. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר in the name of רבי מאיר says she redeems it without a חומש.
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman may not redeem second tithe without adding a fifth. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says in the name of רבי מאיר: a woman may redeem second tithe without adding a fifth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא with a disagreement about whether a woman adds a fifth when redeeming מעשר שני. This sets up the analysis that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally an owner who redeems his own מעשר שני adds a fifth to its value. The question is whether a wife redeeming in this situation counts like the owner. רבי מאיר says she does not have to add the fifth.

keyTerms.meaning: Second tithe, produce eaten in ירושלים or redeemed for money
Redeems; moves the holiness onto money
An added fifth that an owner pays when redeeming his own holy item

phrases.english: A woman does not redeem second tithe
without adding a fifth.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי מֵאִיר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says in the name of Rabbi Meir:

phrases.aramaic: אִשָּׁה פּוֹדָה מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי בְּלֹא חוֹמֶשׁ.
phrases.english: A woman redeems second tithe without adding a fifth.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין אִשָּׁה פּוֹדָה מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי בְּלֹא חוֹמֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new source that will be compared to the earlier slave case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תנא קמא: she must add a חומש. רבי מאיר: she does not add a חומש.

steps.title: What exactly is the case?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what situation the ברייתא is describing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what case the ברייתא means. This sets up a list of possible cases that it will test one by one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whose money is used and whose מעשר it is changes the law. So the גמרא has to pin down the exact case before it can understand the disagreement.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What are the circumstances?

phrases.english: What is the case?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the case behind the ברייתא in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whose money and whose מעשר are involved in the ברייתא's case.

steps.title: Not the husband's money and the husband's tithe
steps.stepSummary: If both the money and the מעשר are the husband's, she is just his agent. Then a חומש is obviously required, so רבי מאיר could not exempt her.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is with the husband's money and the husband's tithe, she is simply acting as the husband's agent!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the first possible case and rejects it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An agent acts in place of the person who sent him. If she uses his money for his מעשר, it is as if the husband redeemed his own מעשר, which needs a חומש. Then no one, not even רבי מאיר, could say she is exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: Agency; acting on someone else's behalf

phrases.english: If you say it is with the husband's money,
and the husband's tithe —
she is just doing the husband's agency?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question of step 2, rejected right away.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The case of the husband's money and the husband's מעשר.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: She would be his agent, so a חומש is clearly needed and רבי מאיר's ruling makes no sense.

steps.title: Not her money and the husband's tithe
steps.stepSummary: If she uses her own money for his מעשר, the פסוק says only 'a man' adds a חומש. So everyone would agree she is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: But rather with her own money and his tithe? The תורה said 'a man,' and not a woman!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a second possible case and rejects it as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק requiring a חומש speaks of 'a man' redeeming his own tithe. A woman redeeming her husband's מעשר with her own money is not covered, so even the תנא קמא would exempt her. The ברייתא would then have no disagreement.

phrases.english: But rather with her own money
and his tithe —
The Torah said "a man," and not a woman!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second answer to step 2, also rejected.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The case of her money and the husband's מעשר.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פסוק already exempts her, so the תנא קמא could not require a חומש.

steps.title: Money given on condition: the opinions seem reversed
steps.stepSummary: The case must be one where someone gave her money on condition that she redeem the מעשר with it. In that case the opinions here are the reverse of what the same חכמים said in the slave case.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, is it not a case like this: another person transferred a maneh to her and said, 'on condition that you redeem the tithe with it'? And we heard them say the opposite!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles on the only case left: money given to her on condition. It then points out a contradiction with the earlier slave case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the slave case, רבי מאיר said the master acquires money given to the slave even with such a condition, and the חכמים said he does not. Here, רבי מאיר seems to say the husband does not acquire the money, since no חומש is needed. The תנא קמא seems to say the husband does acquire it, since a חומש is needed. Each side appears to contradict its own view.

keyTerms.meaning: A sum of one hundred זוז

steps.confusionAlert: The contradiction is not inside this ברייתא. It is between this ברייתא and the earlier slave case, where רבי מאיר held the master acquires money given with a condition.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not a case like this,
where another person transferred a maneh to her,
and said to her:
"on condition that you redeem the tithe with it"?
And we heard them say the opposite!
phrases.notes: This points back to the slave case just before this, where רבי מאיר said the master does get such money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting the other cases, it identifies the remaining case and raises a contradiction.
steps.kashyaTarget: The consistency of רבי מאיר and the חכמים between the slave case and this ברייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the slave case רבי מאיר says the owner acquires conditional gifts. Here he seems to say the husband does not, and the חכמים seem to flip the same way.

steps.title: אביי: switch the opinions
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the opinions in the ברייתא about מעשר should be reversed.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי resolves the contradiction by swapping who says what in the מעשר ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the opinions are swapped, רבי מאיר requires a חומש, because the husband acquired the money. The חכמים exempt her, because he did not. Both sides then match their views in the slave case.

phrases.english: Abaye said: Reverse it.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Switching the opinions in the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא as written contradicts the slave case.
steps.terutzMaskana: With the opinions swapped, each תנא is consistent.

steps.title: רבא: keep the opinions, since the tithe came from her father's house
steps.stepSummary: רבא does not reverse the opinions. The מעשר came to her from her father's house, and רבי מאיר holds מעשר is sacred property, which the husband never acquires.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Actually, do not reverse it. Here we are dealing with tithe that came to her from her father's house. רבי מאיר follows his own reasoning, for he said that tithe is sacred property and the husband does not acquire it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different answer that keeps the ברייתא as written. He explains that the מעשר is hers and not the husband's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר can still hold that the husband acquires the money given to her, like the master in the slave case. But the husband never owned the מעשר, because רבי מאיר treats it as sacred property. So the husband is not redeeming his own מעשר, and no חומש is due.

keyTerms.meaning: Sacred property, belonging to the holy domain

steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers to the contradiction. אביי swaps the opinions. רבא keeps them, saying the מעשר came from her father's house and that רבי מאיר views מעשר as ממון הקדש, so the husband never owns it.
steps.whyThisMatters: רבא's answer depends on רבי מאיר's general view that מעשר is ממון הקדש. That view has effects well beyond this case.

phrases.english: Rava said: Actually, do not reverse it,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָכָא בְּמַעֲשֵׂר דַּאֲתָא מִבֵּי נָשָׁא עָסְקִינַן,
phrases.english: and here we are dealing with tithe that came from her father's house,
and Rabbi Meir follows his own reasoning, for he said:
tithe is sacred property,
and the husband does not acquire it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: An alternative answer to the קשיא of step 5, instead of אביי's swap.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (the מעשר came from her father's house) together with a principle of רבי מאיר
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is about the husband's own מעשר, so it contradicts the slave case.
steps.terutzMaskana: The מעשר is hers, and for רבי מאיר the husband cannot own it, so no חומש is due even with his money.

steps.title: The רבנן hold that מעשר is ordinary property, so she acts as the husband's agent
steps.stepSummary: רבא finishes his answer. The רבנן hold that מעשר is ordinary property, so the husband acquires it. When the wife redeems it, she is his agent and must add a חומש.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן follow their usual view. They say מעשר is ordinary, non-holy property, so the husband acquires it. Therefore she is acting as the husband's agent.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second half of רבא's answer. רבי מאיר exempts her from חומש, and here the גמרא explains why the רבנן obligate her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר holds מעשר is holy property, so the husband never owns it. The מעשר stays hers, so even though the money counts as the husband's, he is not redeeming his own מעשר, and no חומש is due. The רבנן hold מעשר is ordinary property, so the husband does acquire it. She is then redeeming his מעשר as his agent, and the חומש applies.
steps.whatToRemember: רבא does not reverse the opinions. The whole מחלוקת depends on one question: is מעשר holy property or ordinary property? If it is ordinary, the husband acquires it, so she is his agent and pays the חומש. If it is holy, the husband never acquires it, so it stays hers and she does not pay.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis follow their own reasoning, as they say:
It is ordinary property,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the מעשר. 'Ordinary' here means not belonging to the בית המקדש.

phrases.english: and the husband acquires it,
therefore she is acting as the husband's agent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבא's answer from step 7 by explaining the opposing view of the רבנן.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different underlying principle (holy vs. ordinary property)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The opinions seemed to contradict the slave case and would need to be reversed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The opinions do not need to be reversed. Each side follows its own view on whether מעשר is holy property.

steps.title: A ברייתא: a slave goes free through tooth, eye, and limb-tips
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא teaches that an עבד כנעני goes free if his master destroys his tooth, his eye, or the tips of limbs that do not grow back.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: a slave goes free through a tooth, an eye, and limb-tips that do not grow back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting a ברייתא about other ways an עבד כנעני goes free.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה mentions only a tooth and an eye. This ברייתא adds the tips of other limbs, as long as they do not grow back. The next steps ask where that addition comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: tips of limbs (fingers, toes, ears and the like)

phrases.english: A Sage taught: He goes free through a tooth and an eye
phrases.notes: 'He' is an עבד כנעני whose master damaged these body parts.

phrases.english: and through the tips of limbs that do not grow back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, no longer about מעשר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An עבד כנעני goes free through damage to a tooth, an eye, or limb-tips that do not regenerate.

steps.title: Where do we learn the limb-tips from?
steps.stepSummary: Tooth and eye are written in the תורה. The גמרא asks for the source for the limb-tips.
steps.simpleTranslation: Tooth and eye are fine, because they are written in the תורה. But where do we learn the limb-tips from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the ברייתא's extra case, the limb-tips.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'בשלמא... אלא' pattern accepts one part and questions the other. Tooth and eye have a פסוק. The limb-tips do not, so they need a source.

phrases.english: Granted, tooth and eye are written.
But the limb-tips, from where do we know them?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא שֵׁן וָעַיִן כְּתִיבִי, אֶלָּא רָאשֵׁי אֵבָרִים מְנָלַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the ברייתא's ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for freeing a slave over limb-tips.

steps.title: Limb-tips are learned from tooth and eye
steps.stepSummary: Tooth and eye are visible blemishes that do not heal. So any visible blemish that does not heal also frees the slave.
steps.simpleTranslation: They are like tooth and eye. Tooth and eye are visible blemishes that do not come back, so every visible blemish that does not come back works too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that we take the shared features of tooth and eye and apply them to other limbs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is built from two features: the blemish is visible, and it is permanent. Any injury with both features frees the slave, even though only tooth and eye are named.

phrases.english: They are similar to tooth and eye:
just as tooth and eye are visible blemishes
and do not grow back,

phrases.aramaic: אַף כֹּל מוּמִין שֶׁבַּגָּלוּי וְאֵינָן חוֹזְרִין.
phrases.english: so too, all visible blemishes that do not grow back.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Limb-tips are learned from the shared features of tooth and eye: visible and permanent.

steps.title: Aren't tooth and eye two verses that teach the same thing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the derivation. Tooth and eye teach the same law, so they should count as 'two verses that come as one'. Such verses cannot teach other cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let us say tooth and eye are like two verses that come as one. Any two verses that come as one do not teach anything for other cases!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer of step 11 using a known rule of how we learn from פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a rule: if the תורה states the same law twice for two cases, that suggests the law is limited to those cases. Otherwise one case would have been enough to learn from. So the limb-tips should not be learned from tooth and eye.

keyTerms.meaning: two verses teaching the same law
they do not teach for other cases

steps.confusionAlert: This is not about two separate פסוקים contradicting each other. They agree completely. That repetition itself is what limits the law to those cases.

phrases.english: But say that tooth and eye should be
like two verses that come as one,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֹל שְׁנֵי כְתוּבִים הַבָּאִים כְּאֶחָד אֵין מְלַמְּדִין!
phrases.english: and any two verses that come as one do not teach!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵימָא נִיהְווֹ שֵׁן וָעַיִן כִּשְׁנֵי כְתוּבִים הַבָּאִים כְּאֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the derivation given in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: Learning the limb-tips from tooth and eye.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two פסוקים teaching the same law cannot be used to teach other cases, so the limb-tips cannot be learned from them.

steps.title: Both were needed: tooth alone would have been misunderstood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to answer. Tooth and eye are not a true repetition, because each was needed. If only tooth were written, we would have made a mistake.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is necessary. For if the תורה had written only 'tooth', I would have said even...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts explaining that neither tooth nor eye could be learned from the other. The sentence continues in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule of 'two verses that come as one' applies only when the second פסוק was unnecessary. If each case teaches something the other could not, both are needed. Then they can still teach other cases, like the limb-tips.

phrases.english: It is necessary,
for if the Merciful One had written only 'tooth',
I would have said that even

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the challenge of step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: showing each case is needed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Tooth and eye repeat the same law, so they cannot teach other cases.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each was needed, so they are not a true repetition and can teach other cases.
